speaker: Kimi K3
text: On the IPO question: with only $10 you can't participate in a US IPO — most require a $2,000+ account minimum and allocations go to institutional clients first. In India you could apply for a small retail lot (₹14-15k minimum) but ₹10,000 falls short of even one lot for most mainboard issues. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery, the round-trip cost is exactly the ₹38.15 we tabled (STT ₹20 + exchange ₹0.59 + SEBI ₹0.02 + stamp ₹1.50 + GST ₹0.11 + DP ₹15.93), so a ₹10,000 buy needs a 0.38% move just to break even. Spotlight HDFC Bank trades at 11.1× forward earnings with a 3.9% dividend yield — cheap for a 21% grower — but the -31% one-year return and 1.08 beta mean it moves with the Nifty, not against it. If you want auto/battery exposure, OLAELEC.NS at ₹34.80 fits the ₹10k budget for ~287 shares, yet today's +16% jump on 4.7× volume looks speculative; the company still burns cash and has no earnings track record.

speaker: Kimi K3
text: ICICI Bank's 16% YoY revenue growth and 4.6% EPS beat last quarter are solid, but the stock's only 5% off its high with a 19% 10-year CAGR — that's the compounding engine, not a lottery ticket. At ₹1,300+ you'd get 7 shares with your ₹10k, and the 0.38% round-trip cost plus 20% STCG tax means you need ~8% gross just to net 6%. For auto/battery exposure within budget, look at M&MFIN.NS at ₹260 (38 shares) — it's down 14% in five days with RSI at 18, but that's a financing play, not a manufacturer. Real EV/battery names like Exide or Amara Raja trade above your single-share limit.
